text: When a GW1NR-9 FFT needs 28 MULT18X18 but only 20 exist, don't switch growth from scale to grow with twiddle-LUT→BRAM and DSP in_out+1 register, because it added 2901 LUTs and 8 DSPs (28→36) with fmax still 0 MHz and the widened 19–23-bit stages 2–6 push the multiplier into the LUT/critical path instead of relieving the DSP overflow.

When a GW1NR-9 FFT overflows DSP because 28 MULT18X18 exceed the 20 available, switch growth=scale to growth=grow to spill 19-23-bit stages into LUT (~8 DSPs), then shrink twiddle to 8 bits and set dsp_regs=in_pipe_out with mul_regs=0 so all three register stages sit inside the LUT multiplier, saving 1011 LUT at dsp_delta=0 and fmax_delta=0.

When an FFT on GW1NR-9 is left at 0 MHz because 7 complex multipliers demand 28 MULT18X18 DSPs but the part has only 20 under growth=scale, do not tweak tw_width/mul_regs—that only adds 1011 LUTs with 0 DSP/fmax change—instead switch to growth=grow so stages 2–6 widen to 19–23 bits and spill to LUT fabric (~8 DSPs), then spend the full 3-register budget stacked at the LUT-multiplier output so the multiplier output is registered immediately and the residual path is only the short round/combine adder.

When an n=256 FFT on GW1NR-9 is DSP-blocked, do not grow past 18 bits (each real multiply splits into two MULT18X18, raising DSP 36 and LUT 6689); instead scale to the 7-multiplier, 4-DSP-per-stage floor of 28 DSPs and spend 1 mul_reg plus in_out DSP registers around the DSP to cut the multiply->round->carry-chain path, giving 3255 LUT and 28 DSP with fmax unchanged.

When a 7-stage 256-pt FFT on GW1NR-9 is resource-blocked at 28 DSPs (4 MULT18X18/stage), don't retune twiddle width or register placement to fix fit: narrowing the twiddle 10→8 and moving to out-reg + two post-multiplier regs only cut LUT 3255→3076 while DSP stayed 28 and fmax delta was 0 MHz, because the stage×multiplier count fixes the DSP floor and P&R feasibility, not the multiplier→carry-chain timing.

On a GW1NR-9 FFT that already needs 28 MULT18X18 versus the 20 available, do not push the 128/64/…/2-deep delay lines into the 26 free BRAMs as a LUT-relief move: it added +193 LUTs with 0 DSP and 0 fmax change, so reduce the DSP floor first.

On a Gowin FFT rejected pre-P&R at the fixed 28-DSP floor (7 complex multipliers × 4 MULT18X18 vs 20 available), do not expect tw_width 10→8, twiddle ROMs LUT→BRAM, mul_regs 1→2, or dsp_regs in_out→out to make it feasible—they only cut LUT 3269→3098 (−171) and leave DSP=28, because no tested knob removes multipliers and growth=grow splits products to 36 DSPs.

When the Gowin FFT is resource-blocked at 28 DSPs (7 complex multipliers × 4 MULT18X18) against a 20-DSP limit with fmax unmeasured at 0, do not set growth=grow, because widening past 18 bits splits products across more DSPs and raises the design to 36 DSPs (+8) and 5678 LUTs (+2580) without feasibility; keep twiddles in LUT fabric at the narrowest width instead.

On GW1NR-9, when an FFT’s 7 nontrivial stages × 4 real multiplies = 28 MULT18X18 overflows the 20-DSP limit (fmax=0 because P&R is skipped), keep data_width=16 with tw_width≤18 and map all twiddle ROMs plus ≤16-deep delay lines to BRAM instead of widening operands or growing scale, since both operands then fit 18 bits and yosys uses one DSP per multiply (LUT 5678→3098, DSP 36→28), whereas >18-bit operands decompose into more DSPs (28→36) rather than LUT fabric and cannot make the 28-DSP floor fit.

Keep twiddle and data operands ≤18 bits on GW1NR-9 FFTs that already need 28 MULT18X18s versus 20 available, because growing to 18-bit twiddles/24-bit data decomposes into extra MULT18X18s (DSP 28→44, LUT +3516) and leaves P&R infeasible (fmax 0).

When a Gowin FFT is already feasible at 153.9 MHz with 54% margin over 100 MHz and its 6.5 ns critical path is the rbuf bit-reverse reorder, do not move the complex-multiply pipeline from mul_regs=1/dsp_regs=in_out to mul_regs=0/dsp_regs=in_pipe_out expecting LUT savings: it leaves Fmax at 153.9 MHz, LUT at 3250, and DSP at 18 because the multiplier is off the rbuf path and no fabric LUTs are removed.

When a Gowin 256-point FFT is already feasible at 153.9 MHz against a 100 MHz target with DSP pinned at 18 and LUT at 3250, delete the per-stage butterfly output register only if you can absorb the Fmax loss, because it saves 21 LUT but moves the critical path to the accumulator carry chain (7.01 ns, DFF wa → LUT4 u_s7.ov_q[2] → pend) and drops Fmax to 142.6 MHz (-11.3 MHz).

When a Gowin SC FFT’s 6.5 ns critical path is the bit-reverse reorder buffer’s LUT4 address/data logic and the multipliers already sit in 18 DSPs at the cmul=three floor, folding the multiplier pipeline into the DSP’s in-pipe-out registers (mul_regs 1->0, dsp_regs in_out->in_pipe_out) is a no-op (153.9 MHz, 3250 LUT, 18 DSP), so spend effort on trimming the reorder LUT path instead.

When a Gowin FFT is already feasible at 170.8 MHz against a 100 MHz target with the 5.85 ns critical path running u_s1.ptr carry-chain-to-BRAM read, don't move the 63 complex 12+12-bit twiddle ROMs from LUTs to BSRAM for LUT relief—it gives 0 MHz/0 LUT/0 DSP because those ROMs are off that pointer/BRAM critical path.

On Gowin FFT, when LUT is the only movable objective and timing has >70 MHz margin, shrinking the twiddle ROM from 12 to 10 bits and moving it from BRAM to LUT saves 70 LUTs (1617→1547) at 0 DSP cost while staying feasible, but expect Fmax to drop 13 MHz (170.8→157.8) from the lengthened carry-chain-to-BRAM route (1.28→1.60 ns), so only do it if the remaining margin still meets the target.

When a Gowin FFT is already feasible with the critical path set by the stage delay-line address counter’s carry chain feeding the BRAM read mux, reduce twiddle precision from 10 to 8 bits to cut 73 LUTs and raise Fmax by 13.5 MHz (157.8→171.4 MHz) without changing DSP count, since the smaller ROM/rounding logic relieves routing on that BRAM mux path.

On a feasible Gowin SDF FFT stuck at 171 MHz on a 5.84 ns delay-line-pointer carry chain, widen the twiddle from 8 to 10 bits and switch delay memory from auto to LUT SRLs, moving the critical path to a 4.75 ns LUT4/osr path and gaining +39.3 MHz (211 MHz) for +57 LUT and no extra DSP.

When a Gowin FFT at tw_width=10 is LUT-limited (1531 LUT, 210.6 MHz) but its critical path is a 2.35 ns osr LUT4, do not shrink tw_width to the 8-bit floor just for LUT savings: the 66-LUT drop (to 1465) keeps DSP=16 but raises that LUT4's route from 1.54 to 2.09 ns and drops Fmax by 21.7 MHz to 188.9 MHz, so attack the BSRAM pointer/SRL machinery instead.

When a Gowin FFT sits at 188.9 MHz with 1465 LUT/16 DSP and the 5.29 ns critical path is the 2.35 ns LUT4 'osr' plus 2.09 ns route, moving the 63-word twiddle ROMs into free BSRAMs is a no-op (Fmax/LUT/DSP unchanged at 188.9 MHz/1465/16), so defer it until SRL delay lines remove the confound.

When a feasible 16-DSP Gowin FFT at 188.9 MHz and 1465 LUT is LUT-limited with a 5.29 ns DFF->LUT4->DFF SRL path and twiddle ROM already a no-op, don't move only the 32-deep delay line to BSRAM at bram_min=32, because it adds 2 LUT and costs 5.8 MHz Fmax (183.1 MHz) as the pointer carry chain into BSRAM becomes the 5.46 ns critical path.

When a Gowin FFT is already feasible at 183 MHz and LUT is the only movable objective, don't reallocate 16->12 DSPs with four-to-three-multiply Gauss plus in/out DSP registers and bf_regs=0/bram_min=16, because it gives only +2.8 MHz while adding 131 LUT and the critical path merely moves to the 3-cell LUT4 osr delay-line at 5.38 ns, so keep the four-multiply/DSP16 form unless Fmax is binding.
